- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a low sentiment period, cap the peak at 10–15% above recent 7-day average to prevent overshoot.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is below recent history, adjust upward by 3–5% to counteract pessimism bias.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from 14-day moving average, reweight forecast toward recent 7-day trend.  
- If sentiment history shows a sharp drop followed by a rebound, delay forecast correction until sentiment stabilizes (wait 2–3 days).  
- Avoid forecasting below 65% of 30-day historical min unless sentiment is strongly bullish (>0.8) and recent price is trending up.  
- If forecast consistently overestimates true outcome by >5% over 3 consecutive periods, reduce forecast slope by 10–15% for next horizon.
